items.stem: A configuration change was typed but the device still behaves as before. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The candidate configuration was not committed
options.rationale: Correct: Junos changes take effect only after a commit.

options.text: The device needs a full reboot for any change
options.rationale: Most Junos changes apply on commit without a reboot.

options.text: The CLI is in operational mode permanently
options.rationale: You can enter configuration mode to make and commit changes.
Routing policy does not prevent configuration from committing.

items.explanation: Correct: Junos changes take effect only after a commit.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: How is a transit packet handled differently from an exception packet on a Junos device?

options.text: Transit packets are forwarded by the data plane; exception packets go to the routing engine
options.rationale: Correct: the data plane forwards transit traffic while exceptions are punted to the RE.

options.text: Both are always processed by the routing engine
options.rationale: Transit traffic is handled by the forwarding plane, not the RE.
Exception packets are processed by the RE, not simply dropped.

options.text: Transit packets require a commit to forward
options.rationale: Forwarding does not require a configuration commit per packet.

items.explanation: Correct: the data plane forwards transit traffic while exceptions are punted to the RE.

items.stem: Which TWO safeguards let you apply a risky change while protecting against lockout? (Select TWO)

options.text: Use commit confirmed with a rollback timer
options.rationale: Correct: commit confirmed auto-rolls back if not confirmed in time.

options.text: Review the change with show | compare before commit
options.rationale: Correct: comparing candidate vs active config catches mistakes before commit.
Deleting rollback history removes your recovery options.

options.text: Disable the management interface during the change
options.rationale: Disabling management risks the very lockout you want to avoid.

items.explanation: Correct: commit confirmed auto-rolls back if not confirmed in time. Correct: comparing candidate vs active config catches mistakes before commit.
